# Datadog Dashboard Requirements Checklist: Scaffolder Datadog Dashboard Baseline

**Purpose**: Validate requirement quality for Datadog dashboard scaffolding behavior, especially baseline selection, idempotency, and failure semantics
**Created**: 2026-10-19
**Feature**: [Link to spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for first-run provisioning and retry behavior using the same project identity across scaffold reruns? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-010, User Story 1]
- [ ] CHK002 Are all required request elements fully specified, including stable project key, dashboard name, baseline profile choice, and project-specific display values? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements explicit about processing multiple dashboard definitions in one scaffold run, including expected per-item handling? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, User Story 2]
- [ ] CHK004 Are requirements defined for templates that mark dashboard provisioning as required but provide no dashboard definitions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK005 Does the specification define the minimum required shape of a dashboard provisioning result beyond status (for example identifying reference fields)? [Gap, Spec §FR-004]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is "identifiable outcome" defined with concrete fields so readers can determine exactly what must be returned per dashboard? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK007 Is "clear message" for failures quantified with expected content elements (failing definition identifier, reason category, remediation signal)? [Clarity, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "required dashboard content and metadata" unambiguous about which fields are mandatory and which are optional? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "platform-configured Datadog account" defined clearly enough to avoid interpretation drift across environments? [Clarity, Assumption, Spec §FR-009]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK010 Do idempotency requirements align across User Story 1 acceptance scenarios and FR-007 without conflicting update/create expectations? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, User Story 1]
- [ ] CHK011 Do partial-failure semantics remain consistent between FR-005 and User Story 3 Scenario 3 regarding retained successes and step failure? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK012 Are constraints on unmanaged dashboards consistently stated across edge cases, clarifications, and FR-007? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, Edge Case, Clarifications]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK013 Can each functional requirement be objectively evaluated from written acceptance scenarios without adding unstated assumptions? [Measurability, Spec §FR-001..FR-010]
- [ ] CHK014 Are success criteria measurable with explicit data sources, measurement windows, and ownership for collection? [Acceptance Criteria, Ambiguity, Spec §SC-001..SC-004]
- [ ] CHK015 Are error-quality expectations testable at requirements level (actionable, specific, dashboard-identifying) rather than subjective wording? [Measurability, Spec §FR-006, User Story 3]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK016 Are requirements complete for primary, alternate, and retry flows across create, update, and mixed-result batch processing? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-005, Spec §FR-007, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK017 Are exception-flow requirements defined for authorization loss, API unavailability, and malformed baseline definitions? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-006, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK018 Are recovery expectations specified for reruns after partial success so missing dashboards are created and existing managed ones are updated? [Coverage, Recovery, Spec §FR-007, Edge Case]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK019 Are duplicate dashboard names for one project key handled with clearly defined rejection behavior and response detail? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-010, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK020 Is collision behavior with pre-existing unmanaged dashboards fully defined, including non-modification and failure reporting requirements? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-007, Spec §FR-006, Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK021 Are observability requirements for this scaffolder action itself defined (for example logs/metrics needed to audit per-dashboard outcomes)? [Gap, Non-Functional, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK022 Are performance expectations for multi-dashboard runs specified well enough to detect unacceptable scaffolding delays? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [ ] CHK023 Are security and least-privilege requirements defined for Datadog access scope and failure behavior when permissions are insufficient? [Non-Functional, Dependency, Spec §FR-009, Assumptions]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK024 Are external dependency assumptions (single Datadog account, provisioning permissions, baseline ownership) explicitly validated or bounded with fallback behavior? [Dependencies, Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK025 Are responsibilities clearly separated between platform owners and template authors for baseline definition lifecycle and display-value inputs? [Dependencies, Clarity, Spec §Assumptions, User Story 2]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK026 Is an explicit requirement ID-to-acceptance mapping present so each scenario traces back to one or more FR entries without gaps? [Traceability, Gap]
- [ ] CHK027 Are terms such as "configured," "required," and "actionable" consistently defined to avoid multiple interpretations by different teams? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-008]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
